rationale: Two blocking findings: (1) the new import in session-signals.ts uses a deep relative path instead of the project's documented @/ alias (confirmed configured and used elsewhere in the codebase), and (2) the Write path's pre-existing `if (content)` falsy-check still leaves linesAdded undefined for an empty-content Write instead of 0, missing AC2's empty-file requirement even though countContentLines('') itself is correct and unit-tested. All three review lenses (blind, edge-case, acceptance) ran successfully with parseable output; acceptance criteria were available. 3 additional concerns were triaged as dismiss/defer (pre-existing content-type-safety risk at the Write call site and inside the now-exported countContentLines, out-of-scope sibling-plugin duplicate bugs, no bare-CR line-ending test) — real but not introduced by this diff or not required by the stated acceptance criteria, so not blocking. AC5 (downstream Overview/Efficiency/Repositories display) is marked partial — not independently demonstrated by a test in this diff — but judged low-risk and not raised as a blocking finding, since technical-analysis.md confirms downstream consumers only sum/display the already-corrected linesAdded value with no separate aggregation defect.

findings.title: New import uses deep relative path instead of @/ alias
findings.problem: The diff adds `import { countContentLines } from '../../../../utils/file-operations.js';` — a brand-new import statement (this file previously had zero imports) written as a 4-level deep relative path.
findings.impact: Violates the project's own documented convention (AGENTS.md Common Pitfalls: 'Deep relative imports (../../..)' -> 'Use @/ alias'), which is confirmed configured (tsconfig.json paths) and actively used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. statusline.ts).

findings.title: Empty-content Write still leaves linesAdded undefined, not 0
findings.problem: `const content = res.content || res.file?.content || inp.content; if (content) { fileOp.linesAdded = countContentLines(content); }` — the `if (content)` guard treats an empty string as falsy, so countContentLines is never called when Write content is ''.
findings.impact: AC2 explicitly requires empty files to be handled correctly for the Write tool. countContentLines('') correctly returns 0 and is unit-tested in isolation, but the full extraction pipeline never reaches that call for an empty-content Write, leaving linesAdded undefined instead of 0.
findings.recommendation: Guard on definedness instead of truthiness, e.g. `if (content !== undefined) { fileOp.linesAdded = countContentLines(content); }`, and add a test asserting `extractClaudeFileOperation('Write', { content: '' }, { content: '' })` yields `linesAdded: 0`.
